title: Mount Abu: Rajasthan’s Only Hill Station
content:
Mount Abu

Mount Abu, located in the Aravalli Range, is Rajasthan’s only hill station and a refreshing escape from the desert heat. Situated at about 1,220 meters above sea level, it offers pleasant weather, lush landscapes, and a peaceful vibe that attracts tourists year-round.

One of the top attractions is the Dilwara Jain Temples, known for their exquisite marble carvings and spiritual significance. Equally popular is Nakki Lake, perfect for a relaxing boat ride with scenic views and iconic landmarks like Toad Rock.

For sunset lovers, Sunset Point and Honeymoon Point offer stunning views of the surrounding hills. Adventure seekers can explore the Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary, home to leopards, foxes, and a variety of bird species. 

The town also offers vibrant markets, delicious local food (don’t miss Rabri), and a mix of luxury and budget-friendly accommodations.

You can reach Mount Abu via Abu Road railway station (28 km away), or by road from cities like Udaipur and Ahmedabad.

Whether you're looking for nature, culture, or a peaceful getaway, Mount Abu is the perfect hill retreat in the heart of Rajasthan.

Top Places to visit in Mount Abu

1.Nakki Lake - The Heart of Mount Abu

 

Nakki Lake, located in the hill station of Mount Abu, Rajasthan, is a beautiful and serene man-made lake surrounded by lush green hills, rocky landscapes, and vibrant gardens. Known as the “Love Lake” of Mount Abu, it is believed to have been dug out by gods using their nails (nakh), which is how it got its name.

The lake is a favorite spot for both tourists and locals, offering boating experiences that let you enjoy the stunning views of the surrounding hills and the famous Toad Rock nearby. In the evening, the lake comes alive with colorful lights, food stalls, and a lively atmosphere, making it a perfect place for families, couples, and photographers.

With its calm waters, scenic beauty, and mythological charm, Nakki Lake is undoubtedly the soul of Mount Abu and a must-visit attraction.

  • Entry Fee: Free (boating charges apply: ₹50-₹200 approx., depending on boat type)
  • Timings: 9:30 AM - 6:00 PM (boating hours) | Lake open all day
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March (pleasant weather for sightseeing and boating)

 

2. Guru Shikhar - The Highest Peak of Aravalli

 

Guru Shikhar, the highest peak of the Aravalli Range, is one of the most popular attractions in Mount Abu, Rajasthan. Situated at an altitude of 1,722 meters (5,650 feet), it offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding hills, forests, and valleys, making it a paradise for nature lovers and trekkers.

The peak is named after Guru Dattatreya, a revered sage considered an incarnation of Lord Vishnu, Lord Brahma, and Lord Shiva. The Guru Dattatreya Temple, located at the summit, is a sacred site where devotees come to seek blessings. The journey to the top involves a short trek with steps leading up, and the cool breeze with scenic landscapes makes it an enjoyable climb.

Guru Shikhar is not just a spiritual destination but also a scenic spot for adventure seekers, photographers, and peace lovers who want to enjoy Mount Abu’s natural beauty from the highest point.

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Timings: 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March for clear skies and pleasant weather

 

3. Toad Rock View Point – The Iconic Rock Formation of Mount Abu

 

Toad Rock, perched on a hill near Nakki Lake, is one of the most famous landmarks of Mount Abu. The rock formation looks like a giant toad ready to jump into the lake, which is how it got its name. To reach the viewpoint, visitors climb a short trek of stone steps, and once at the top, they are rewarded with breathtaking views of Nakki Lake and the surrounding Aravalli hills. It is a favorite spot for nature lovers, photographers, and those who enjoy a bit of adventure with scenic beauty.

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Timings: Open all day
  • Best Time to Visit: Sunrise and sunset for the most beautiful views

 

4. Dilwara Jain Temple - A Marvel of Marble Architecture

 

The Dilwara Jain Temples, located about 2.5 km from Mount Abu, are world-renowned for their stunning marble architecture and intricate carvings. Built between the 11th and 13th centuries, these temples are dedicated to various Jain Tirthankaras and are considered among the most beautiful Jain temples in India.

The five main temples are Vimal Vasahi, Luna Vasahi, Pittalhar, Parshvanath, and Mahavir Swami, each showcasing breathtaking artistry with detailed pillars, ceilings, and sculptures carved from white marble. Despite their grandeur, the temples maintain a sense of serenity and spirituality, making them a must-visit for both devotees and travelers interested in art and history.

The peaceful surroundings, combined with the temple’s intricate craftsmanship, make Dilwara Temples not just a religious site but also a masterpiece of Indian architecture.

  • Entry Fee: Free (Donations accepted)
  • Timings: 6:00 AM – 6:00 PM (for devotees) | 12:00 PM – 5:00 PM (for tourists)
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March for pleasant weather
  • Photography: Not allowed inside the temple premises

 

5. Mount Abu Sanctuary - A Wildlife Haven in the Aravallis

 

The Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary, located in the Aravalli Hills, is a paradise for nature lovers and wildlife enthusiasts. Spread over 288 square kilometers, it is home to rich flora, fauna, and scenic landscapes. The sanctuary is especially famous for its orchids, bamboo thickets, and medicinal plants, along with beautiful viewpoints that offer breathtaking views of the hills.

Wildlife lovers can spot leopards, hyenas, foxes, jungle cats, porcupines, and Indian civets, while birdwatchers can enjoy seeing species like grey jungle fowl, peacocks, and migratory birds. The sanctuary is also known for its diverse plant life, with over 800 species of flowering plants, making it one of the greenest patches in Rajasthan.

It is a perfect spot for trekking, photography, and experiencing the natural beauty of Mount Abu beyond its temples and lakes.

  • Entry Fee: ₹50 (Indians), ₹300 (Foreigners) approx.
  • Safari Charges: ₹300-₹600 per person (Jeep Safari)
  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 5:30 PM
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March (for pleasant weather and better wildlife sightings)

 

6. Peace Park - A Place of Meditation and Serenity

 

Peace Park, managed by the Brahma Kumaris, is a serene retreat located between the Guru Shikhar and Achalgarh Fort in Mount Abu. Surrounded by the scenic Aravalli Hills, this beautifully maintained park is designed to provide visitors with an atmosphere of peace, relaxation, and spiritual learning.

The park features lush gardens, meditation spots, rock formations, and a variety of plants and flowers, making it a refreshing escape from the busy tourist areas. Visitors can join guided meditation sessions, spiritual lectures, and educational tours that help them connect with inner peace and mindfulness.

Peace Park is not just for those seeking spirituality-it is also a great place for families and nature lovers to enjoy the tranquil environment, fresh air, and scenic views.

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Timings: 8:00 AM - 7:00 PM
  • Best Time to Visit: Morning or evening for meditation and relaxation

 

7. Lal Mandir - A Simple Yet Sacred Temple

 

Lal Mandir is a small yet significant Jain temple located near the entrance of the famous Dilwara Jain Temples in Mount Abu. Dedicated to Lord Adinath, the first Jain Tirthankara, this temple is known for its simplicity, peaceful atmosphere, and spiritual importance.

Unlike the grand architecture of Dilwara, Lal Mandir is modest in design, painted in red (hence the name “Lal Mandir”), and provides a serene space for quiet prayers and meditation. Devotees and visitors come here to seek blessings, enjoy the calm environment, and experience the deep spiritual energy that the temple radiates.

For those exploring Mount Abu’s religious heritage, Lal Mandir is a hidden gem that offers a glimpse into the devotion and faith of the Jain community.

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Timings: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Best Time to Visit: Morning or evening for peaceful prayers

8. Trevor’s Tank - A Nature Lover’s Paradise

 

Trevor’s Tank, also known as Trevor’s Crocodile Park, is a popular nature spot located about 5 km from Mount Abu town. Built by the British engineer Trevor, this artificial tank is surrounded by lush greenery and rocky hills, making it a perfect escape for nature lovers, birdwatchers, and wildlife enthusiasts.

The park is especially famous for its crocodiles, which can often be spotted basking near the tank. It is also home to various species of birds like pigeons, peacocks, and migratory birds, making it a favorite destination for birdwatching and photography. The peaceful surroundings and dense forests provide an excellent opportunity for picnics and short hikes.

Trevor’s Tank is ideal for travelers seeking a mix of wildlife, nature, and tranquility away from the busy tourist areas of Mount Abu.

  • Entry Fee: ₹30 (Indians), ₹60 (Foreigners) approx.
  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Best Time to Visit: November to March (cool weather and better chances of spotting wildlife)

9. Achleshwar Mahadev Temple - A Sacred Shiva Shrine

 

The Achleshwar Mahadev Temple, located near Achalgarh Fort in Mount Abu, is a revered Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. This ancient temple is believed to house a naturally occurring Shiva Linga, which is considered to be self-manifested and highly sacred.

According to legend, the temple is built around a pit that is said to be bottomless, symbolizing the infinite power of Lord Shiva. The temple complex also features beautiful sculptures, idols of deities, and a brass Nandi (bull) facing the Shiva Linga. The peaceful surroundings, combined with the temple’s mythological significance, make it a must-visit for devotees and spiritual seekers.

Nestled amidst the scenic Aravalli Hills, Achleshwar Mahadev Temple offers not only a spiritual experience but also stunning views of the surrounding landscape, making it a favorite spot for both pilgrims and travelers.

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Timings: 5:00 AM - 7:00 PM
  • Best Time to Visit: Early morning or evening for prayers and a serene atmosphere

10. Achalgarh Fort - A Historic Rajput Stronghold

 

Achalgarh Fort, located about 11 km from Mount Abu, is a historic fort built originally by the Paramara dynasty and later renovated in the 15th century by Rana Kumbha of Mewar. Perched on a hilltop, the fort offers a blend of history, spirituality, and scenic beauty, making it a must-visit attraction for travelers.

The fort houses the famous Achleshwar Mahadev Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva, where a naturally occurring Shiva Linga is worshipped. The fort walls, old gates, and temple structures still reflect the grandeur of Rajput architecture. Visitors can also enjoy panoramic views of the Aravalli Hills and surrounding landscapes, which make the fort a favorite among history lovers and photographers.

Though in partial ruins today, Achalgarh Fort continues to attract tourists for its mythological significance, architectural charm, and peaceful setting.

  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Timings: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March for pleasant weather
excerpt: Mount Abu is Rajasthan’s only hill station, offering cool weather, scenic views, and spiritual sites like the Dilwara Jain Temples. Popular attractions include Nakki Lake, Sunset Point, and the Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary. It’s a perfect getaway for families, couples, and nature lovers.
